explanation: A deacon sent to preach the gospel, known for his teaching about Jesus and baptizing an Ethiopian eunuch.
An ethnic group from Africa south of Egypt; in this chapter, it refers to a high-ranking court official who was reading the prophet Isaiah.
The act of immersing someone in water as a sign of faith and cleansing, performed by Philip on the eunuch.
People from the region of Samaria; many were baptized after hearing Philip's preaching about the kingdom of God.
A man known as a sorcerer in Samaria who later tried to buy the power to give the Holy Spirit with money (simony).
The use of magical or supernatural tricks to impress people, which Simon practiced before he was baptized.
The Holy Spirit who came upon believers after the apostles laid hands on them in Samaria.
Place where Peter and other disciples were imprisoned by King Agrippa; from here Peter was rescued by a miracle.
A heavenly messenger who led Peter out of prison during a nighttime rescue.
